taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Ulakwo, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 14.369 | 0.124 | 0.12415
2 | 15.965 | 8.25 | 9.665
3 | 4591.4 | 27.074 | 47.738
4 | 5101.5 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Ulakwo, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Ulakwo, Etche LGA**

The VES interpretation at Ulakwo reveals a four-layer subsurface sequence with resistivities increasing progressively with depth. Layer 1 (14.369 Ω·m, 0.124 m thick) is underlain by Layer 2 (15.965 Ω·m, 8.25 m thick, base at 9.665 m), followed by Layer 3 (4591.4 Ω·m, 27.074 m thick, base at 47.738 m), and a resistive basal Layer 4 (5101.5 Ω·m).

Applying the curve-type convention: Layers 1-2-3 give r1 < r2 < r3 → A; Layers 2-3-4 give r2 < r3 < r4 → A. The resulting two-letter sequence (AA) simplifies to a single A-type curve, consistent with a continuously increasing resistivity profile with depth—likely indicating a transition from weathered/lateritic overburden to competent, resistive basement material.

This matches the on-file classification of A-type for this station. No discrepancy was found between the computed curve type and the filed label.

{"curve_type_stated": "AA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
